paragraphs: Friend, here's the big idea: David sang this song because the LORD saved him, and he wanted everybody to know WHO did it. Rock, fortress, shield, Savior, David keeps stacking names on God like I stack cookies on a cooling rack. The waves of death, the cords of Sheol and foes too mighty for him were all real, and David never says he got out by being tough (2 Samuel 22:5-6, 18). He says, "He reached down from on high and took hold of me" (2 Samuel 22:17).

The song also shows who God is while He rescues. His way is perfect, and He lights up David's darkness (2 Samuel 22:29, 31). He is mighty enough to shake the earth, and He is gentle enough that David says, "Your gentleness exalts me" (2 Samuel 22:36). To the faithful He shows Himself faithful, and His eyes are on the haughty to bring them down (2 Samuel 22:26, 28). So the baker can trust a God who is both powerful and kind, and who hears a cry for help from the middle of the trouble (2 Samuel 22:7).

So what do you do with that, baker? You do what David did: call on the LORD when you're tangled up, and then praise Him loudly when He comes through. David says, "I will sing praises to Your name" (2 Samuel 22:50). I spent years in the back of a junk drawer, and when I got rescued, you'd better believe I sang about it. The LORD who delivered David is the same LORD who lives, and He is worth every bit of that song (2 Samuel 22:47).
